_meta.source: MOE pages read directly on 2026-11-11: school fees and its fee checker data, financial assistance and its eligibility checker data, Edusave, Post-Secondary Education Account, Higher Education Student Loan, and the 16 October 2025 press release on revised income criteria and bursary amounts. Search extracts only for the autonomous universities, the arts institutions, independent schools, CPF and the self help groups, whose own sites this build could not reach
_meta.units: Singapore dollars, for a Singapore Citizen, before assistance
_meta.notes: Re-checked 2026-11-11. A row with `checked` was read on moe.gov.sg that day and carries no `status`, because the money sweep accepts no status but provisional. A row with `status: provisional` rests at least partly on a search extract or on nothing published: the independent school fee (Hwa Chong and ACS Independent figures from a search extract), the arts institution fee (one LASALLE diploma at 5,490 from a search extract; no NAFA figure found), the university band (NTU's own page and a third party guide, both by search extract), the CPF Education Loan Scheme terms (name confirmed on moe.gov.sg, limits from a search summary of cpf.gov.sg), the self help groups (search extracts) and the school's own fund (MOE confirms it exists and is decided case by case; nothing more is published). Changed on this pass: the Tuition Fee Loan became the Higher Education Student Loan on 29 July 2026; the CPF Education Scheme is the CPF Education Loan Scheme; standard and second tier miscellaneous fees merged into one fee on 1 January 2024; MOE FAS and bursary income limits rose from Academic Year 2026; Edusave awards are paid by PayNow and not into the account; a 10,000 top up to the Post-Secondary Education Account at 17 starts with those turning 17 in 2026. Not found and so not stated: any 2027 fee change for citizens, an ITE registration fee, how often MOE FAS is renewed, bursary deadlines, and whether a self help group bursary can be held with another. Costs are listed before help on purpose, because a page that opened with reassurance would read as a sales pitch. The four truths at the end are the guidance; the tables are the evidence for them.

costs.label: Secondary school, government or government aided
costs.misc: Miscellaneous fees of 20 a month, payable from Edusave
costs.note: For a Singapore Citizen in 2026, so 25 a month in all. Autonomous schools add 3 to 18. Permanent Residents and international students pay published higher rates.

costs.label: Independent school
costs.misc: Varies by school, and published by each
costs.note: The MOE Independent School Bursary covers part of this for households earning up to 12,000 a month, or 3,000 per person.

costs.label: Junior college or Millennia Institute
costs.misc: Miscellaneous fees of 27 a month, so 33 in all
costs.note: Three years at Millennia Institute rather than two, so the total is one more year of the same small number.

costs.label: ITE, Higher Nitec
costs.misc: Plus supplementary fees for examinations, insurance and the like
costs.note: For the 2026 cohort, the same every year of the course. At the first bursary tier the fee is fully covered, with 1,850 a year on top.

costs.label: Polytechnic diploma
costs.misc: Three years for most diplomas, so budget for three
costs.note: For the 2026 cohort, before any bursary. At the first bursary tier the bursary is 3,050 a year.

costs.label: Arts institution diploma or degree
costs.misc: Materials and studio costs are real and are not in the fee
costs.note: Published per course. The government bursaries cover NAFA and LASALLE too, and each has its own schemes. Materials are the cost families forget.

costs.label: Degree at a local autonomous university
costs.misc: More for medicine and dentistry. Fees differ by university and course
costs.note: Subsidised rate for a Singapore Citizen. The Higher Education Student Loan covers up to 90 percent of it, interest free while studying.

help.label: MOE Financial Assistance Scheme
help.what: School fees and all miscellaneous fees, textbooks, uniforms, and subsidies for transport and meals.
help.who: Singapore Citizens in government and government aided schools, with household income up to 4,000 a month, or 1,000 per person.
help.howMuch: In practice this takes the cost of secondary school close to nothing.
help.howToGet: Apply online, or hand the MOE FAS form to the school. One form covers brothers and sisters in other schools.

help.label: Edusave
help.what: An account in the student's own name, topped up every year until the end of secondary school, for miscellaneous fees and enrichment.
help.who: Every Singapore Citizen in school. Nothing to apply for.
help.howMuch: 290 a year for a secondary student. Edusave awards are separate and are paid to the student's bank account by PayNow.
help.howToGet: It is already there. A parent can check the balance on the Student Finance System with Singpass.

help.label: Post Secondary Education Account
help.what: Where the Edusave balance goes in the year the student turns 17, or on leaving an MOE funded school if that is later.
help.who: Singapore Citizens. It pays ITE, polytechnic, arts and university fees, a sibling's too. It does not pay JC or MI costs.
help.howMuch: Whatever Edusave was left, plus a 10,000 top up in the year the student turns 17, from 2026.
help.howToGet: The account is automatic. To pay fees from it, set up a Standing Order for the institution on the Student Finance System.

help.label: Government bursaries at ITE, polytechnic and university
help.what: Money that reduces the fee and does not have to be paid back.
help.who: Four income tiers, up to a household income of 12,000 a month, or 3,000 per person.
help.howMuch: A year, first tier to fourth. ITE: fees plus 1,850, down to 490. Diploma: 3,050 to 950. Degree: 6,300 to 1,350.
help.howToGet: Applied for through the institution's financial aid office. Each institution has its own procedure, so ask on enrolling.

help.label: Higher Education Student Loan
help.what: A loan for subsidised diploma and degree fees, from ITE to university. It replaced the Tuition Fee Loan in July 2026.
help.who: Available broadly, not only on low income. The last 10 percent and a living allowance are income tested.
help.howMuch: Up to 90 percent of the fee, with no interest charged while still studying.
help.howToGet: On the StudentLoanSG portal with Singpass, in the window each institution sets.

help.label: CPF Education Loan Scheme
help.what: Paying fees from a parent's or a sibling's CPF Ordinary Account, repaid with interest after graduating.
help.who: Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents on full time courses at approved institutions in Singapore.
help.howMuch: Up to a share of the account balance, per the scheme's limits.
help.howToGet: An application through CPF, with the student agreeing to repay.

help.label: The self help groups and community funds
help.what: Bursaries and tuition support from CDAC, MENDAKI, SINDA and the Eurasian Association.
help.who: By community, and each publishes its own criteria.
help.howMuch: Varies by group. MENDAKI's tertiary fee subsidy adds to the national schemes.
help.howToGet: Directly, and separately from the school. Ask, because nobody will offer.

help.label: The school's own welfare fund
help.what: The quiet money for a camp fee, a trip, a pair of shoes, a laptop.
help.who: Anybody in the school with a need.
help.howMuch: No published amount. The school decides each request case by case.
help.howToGet: Ask the form teacher, the year head or the general office.

help.label: SkillsFuture Credit, later
help.what: Credit for courses across a working life, with a larger top up in mid career.
help.who: Singapore Citizens, from twenty five, with the mid career top up from forty.
help.howMuch: 500 at 25 and 4,000 in the year of turning 40. Neither expires.
help.howToGet: Nothing to apply for. It sits in an account until it is used.

truths.head: The fee is not the barrier it looks like
truths.body: Every route after secondary school has a bursary attached to it, and the income tiers reach further up than families expect. The most expensive route also has the largest loan behind it, interest free while studying.

truths.head: Some arrives. Most of it is asked for
truths.body: Edusave, the Post Secondary Education Account and SkillsFuture Credit arrive without a form. The Financial Assistance Scheme, the bursaries and the loan are applied for, and a family that does not know a name does not apply.

truths.head: A low fee is not a low ambition
truths.body: At 530 a year, ITE costs less than a polytechnic, an arts institution or a university, and a Higher Nitec takes three years. Earning sooner is a real advantage, and it is no argument against the other routes.

truths.head: Money is a reason to ask, not to stop
truths.body: A family that decides a route is unaffordable without asking has closed a door the system left open. The ECG counsellor and the school's general office both know exactly which forms apply.
